contexts.text: See Faith.
The just nation keeping faithfulnesses ().
The salvation of the faithful, and the damnation of the unfaithful. Treated of.
The faithful are judged from good, and the unfaithful from truth. Signified.
The Africans want to be called the obedient, but not the faithful. They say that Christians can be called the faithful, because they have the doctrine of faith...
(The Rider on the white horse) is called faithful, etc. from good. WH 1:2.
It treats here of the salvation of the faithful: the faithful are the pots, being so called on account of the reception of good from the Lord...
It treats of the salvation of the faithful...
Act sincerely and faithfully...
See Sincerity. DLife 84:2.
Be thou faithful unto death () = the reception and acknowledgement of Truths even until falsities are removed. ( = permanence in truths to the end. AE 125.)
In the natural sense it means that, to the end of life, we should not go back from faithfulness.
Under Choose, see this reference.
The faithful = those who have faith in the Lord.

Faithful and true () = the Divine good and the Divine truth. Faithful = the Divine good, because this is faithful. Faithful, when men are treated of, = one who is in the Third Heaven; thus who is in celestial good.
On the misfortunes of the faithful.
He is the faithful witness () = from Whom is all truth in Heaven... AE 228.
Keeping faithfulnesses = him who is thence in truths.
The just nation keeping faithfulnesses = those who are in good and thence in truths.
Therefore it is said... Ye have been faithful over a few things ().
The faithful who have suffered temptations for the sake of these truths. Signified.
The faithful () = those who are in the faith of charity... The Angels of the First Heaven, who are in the faith of charity, are called faithful.
Fidelity mentioned. DWis 12. 4.
The elevation of the faithful to God, from whom was made a New Heaven; and the removal of the unfaithful from God, from whom was made a new Hell.
